name: Vorderhornbach
kurzbeschreibung: Charming scattered hamlet in the Lechtal valley, surrounded by picturesque farms and untouched Lechtaler nature.
beschreibung:
Überblick

The idyllic mountain village of Vorderhornbach is situated at an altitude of 974 metres above sea level in the middle Lech Valley in the Reutte district, nestling at the foot of the dramatic Hornbach chain of the Allgäu Alps. Home to approximately 260 residents, this peaceful settlement at the mouth of the tributary Hornbach Valley is among the quietest communities in the Außerfern region. The village rests on a gently sloping alluvial cone where the pristine waters of the Hornbach stream merge into the wild River Lech. Vorderhornbach forms an essential part of the Nature Park Tiroler Lech, safeguarding one of Central Europe's last genuine wild river environments with sprawling gravel banks, riparian woodlands, and rare flora. Visitors seeking authentic alpine tranquility will discover a genuine sanctuary here.

Geschichte

Permanent settlement in the upper and middle Lech Valley developed during the High Middle Ages, driven by pioneers from the neighbouring Allgäu and Inn Valley regions. Vorderhornbach was documented during the 13th and 14th centuries in connection with feudal clearing estates, with its name deriving from the rushing Hornbach torrent. For generations, local families subsisted through challenging mountain farming and timber rafting on the Lech, shipping logs downriver towards Augsburg and Donauwörth. In addition, seasonal migration as skilled masons and plasterers played a major role in village survival during the 18th and 19th centuries. The Baroque church of St. John the Baptist was erected in 1738, housing fine historic altars and ceiling frescoes. The village has maintained its authentic architectural character with timber-clad alpine farmsteads.

Anreise

Vorderhornbach is accessible via the scenic highway network of the Außerfern. From the north and east, travel proceeds via Reutte along the Lechtal federal road B198, easily reached through the Füssen border tunnel or via the Fernpass road B179. Approaching from Vorarlberg and the Arlberg area in the snow-free season, the B198 provides access via the Bregenzerwald and Warth. Rail passengers travel to the train station in Reutte in Tirol, where regular regional buses on the Lechtal route connect directly to the village centre. Furthermore, long-distance hikers frequently reach the village on foot along the renowned Lechweg trail.

Tipps

A prime summer attraction is the 'Bad Horn' natural bathing pond (Badino), an eco-friendly outdoor pool with chemical-free natural water filtration, sunbathing lawns, jumping rocks, and splendid mountain vistas. Hikers on the celebrated Lechweg trail can explore the braided channels and gravel banks of the wild Lech river corridor directly beside the village. An excursion into the secluded Hornbach Valley leads to tranquil alpine pastures such as the Schönecker Alm and rewarding alpine ascents up the Klimmspitze. In winter, meticulously groomed cross-country tracks connecting into the extensive Lechtal network and quiet winter walking routes offer wonderful snowy recreation.
